principle: Risk magnitude and reliability are separate outputs. Reliability must never multiply or silently modify the GRI risk score.

resolution_coverage.definition: Fraction of applicable dimensions for which a quantitative point estimate is available.

breadth.definition: Number of independently applicable GRI dimensions represented by quantitative point estimates.
breadth.warning: Breadth is descriptive and does not imply that all seven dimensions should apply to every case.

evidence_profile.definition: Counts of evidence classes contributing to quantitative point estimates.

leave_one_dimension_out.definition: Maximum absolute change in arithmetic composite after removal of one quantitatively scored dimension.

aggregation_rank_stability.definition: Whether case ordering is preserved across prespecified arithmetic, geometric and RMS aggregation alternatives.
aggregation_rank_stability.interpretation: Corpus-level robustness diagnostic, not confidence interval.

provenance_completeness.definition: Fraction of quantitatively scored dimensions containing non-empty source provenance.

forbidden_interpretations: Reliability is probability that GRI is correct.
Evidence class is a numerical risk weight.
Leave-one-out range is a confidence interval.
Full resolution coverage means comprehensive lifecycle coverage.
